proposal.summary: The initial request (SH-CX, CL-01) was a chatbot to explain parcel lateness as a communication gap. Investigation instead found 300 of 1000 orders (30%) late at the 'handover' stage (E-01), and that this traces to the WMS RELEASE-BATCH job failing in 21 of 30 runs, releasing 290 orders only after carrier pickup already occurred (E-04) — a warehouse release-timing failure, not a communication gap or primarily a carrier delay, per the accepted problem definition PD-1 (gate_result CONDITIONAL_PASS). A competing claim that carrier pickup running 2h late is the cause (SH-LOG, CL-02/E-03) is directionally consistent with a measured 2.0h median pickup delay (E-02, E-06) but that delay is uniform across all 6 scheduling slots (E-06), undermining confidence that rescheduling pickups would fix it. The release decision is HOLD: a critical open verification obligation (VOB-R-4) intersects the proposed release scope at push_pickup_schedule:pickup-sched, so this action cannot proceed as scoped.
key_points: Root problem per PD-1: handover-stage lateness (300/1000, E-01) is driven by RELEASE-BATCH job failures (21/30 runs, E-04) causing 290 orders to be released only after pickup already happened (E-04), not by carrier pickup delay or a customer-communication gap.

Hypothesis H-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE is SUPPORTED (by E-04); H-CARRIER-SCHEDULE-MISMATCH, H-HANDOFF-FAILURE, and H-WAREHOUSE-DELAY are REJECTED, and stakeholder claims CL-01 (communication gap) and CL-02 (carrier delay) are both marked CONTRADICTED.

The release decision is HOLD because critical VOB-R-4 intersects the release scope at push_pickup_schedule:pickup-sched: it questions whether changing the pickup schedule would reduce delay, given pickup_by_slot (E-06) shows an identical 2.0h delay across all 6 slots rather than slot-specific variation.

DA-WMS (the source of E-04) has UNKNOWN completeness, and an earlier ACCESS_PENDING hold was recorded on a wms-jobs query signature (A-WMS-DATA-COMPLETENESS), so confidence in E-04-based remedies is undermined.
The tool_health of pickup-sched is UNKNOWN at runtime, adding execution risk to the push_pickup_schedule action even if it were approved.

A-RELEASE-BATCH-DOMINANT-CAUSE is unverified — it is assumed rather than confirmed that RELEASE-BATCH failure dominates over the measured 2h carrier pickup delay (E-02), so push_pickup_schedule may address only a secondary factor and would not close SC-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE-FIXED or SC-ORDERS-RELEASED-AFTER-PICKUP.

The release scope excludes diagnose_release_batch_failures and correlate_release_timing_with_handover_lateness, which are needed to actually fix or confirm the root cause, so even if released the current scope cannot satisfy two of the three success criteria.
